CheckTitle: Ensure IAM role trust policies do not allow overly permissive principal assumptions
Description: IAM role trust policies must not use wildcard principals ('*') in the Principal element that allow any entity (unauthenticated or authenticated) to assume the role. Trust policies must specify explicit principals (AWS accounts, IAM principals, or specific services).
Risk: A trust policy with Principal: '*' allows any AWS principal in any account to attempt to assume the role. Combined with lax conditions, this can enable cross-account unauthorized role assumption, a well-documented AWS privilege escalation vector.
Remediation: Restrict role trust policies to explicit, named principals. Add aws:PrincipalOrgID or aws:PrincipalAccount conditions to limit assumption to your organization's accounts. Use sts:ExternalId for third-party cross-account roles.
SeverityBasis: AWS IAM documentation — Security best practices in IAM (restrict trust policy principals to explicit entities); NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 AC-3 (Access Enforcement), SC-11 (Trusted Path). High severity reflects that wildcard trust enables direct unauthorized role assumption from any AWS principal.
AuthoritativeSource: AWS IAM documentation — Roles and trust policies; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5
CISControl: N/A — permissive trust policy detection is not individually enumerated in CIS AWS 3.0.0
